citations.review_text:
Where is the Switzerland or Japan national team ?
I don't wanna play with those mainstream national team.

About gameplay, I prefer Fifa 2006.

About graphics, seems very unnatural and robotic.

EA SPORTS FC 25 has been a very enjoyable football game for me. The overall gameplay feels smooth, responsive, and fun to play. Passing, shooting, dribbling, and player movement all feel good, and I have spent many enjoyable hours playing tournaments and different game modes.

One thing I did not like is that the Brazil national team is not fully available in Tournament Mode, which was disappointing because I enjoy playing international competitions. However, this did not stop me from enjoying the game overall.

What I appreciate most is EA's pricing strategy. Every year, the latest FC games become available at very affordable prices during sales, allowing more players to enjoy them. I bought FC 25 for only ₹200 during a sale, which was incredible value for money.

For the price I paid, I have absolutely no complaints. The gameplay is enjoyable, the content is good, and I have had a great time with it. If you are looking for a fun football game at a discounted price, FC 25 is definitely worth picking up.

Verdict: Recommended.
Feel like these games are more showy and look cooler but i prefer the older versions. Simple fact i cant play or manage the Mexican league made me regret buying this game.

I’m honestly not happy with EA Sports FC 25.

This game is basically surviving on licenses and nothing else. Career Mode is decent at best. It’s playable, but there’s nothing there that really pulls you back in for the long run. Yes, there are loads of competitions and official content, but content alone doesn’t make a good football game.

The gameplay is where it completely falls apart. The ball feels weightless, like you’re kicking a plastic ball around. Passing, shooting, movement, nothing feels natural or satisfying. The physics are poor and matches feel floaty instead of grounded.

I should also be clear about one thing. I am an offline player, so I’m least bothered about FUT. Ultimate Team does absolutely nothing for me, and it doesn’t excuse how bad the core gameplay feels in offline modes.

What really killed the experience for me:

No Brazil national team
No Neymar anywhere in the entire roster

For a game that sells itself on authenticity, that’s a massive disappointment.

Now EA Sports FC 26 is on sale for $1.58. Honestly, even if someone gave it to me for free, I still wouldn’t play it.

At this point, I’m just hoping Konami eFootball eventually releases a proper paid version with strong, realistic gameplay. Until then, I’ll stick with their live service mess, because even that feels better than this.

EA Sports FC 25 successfully refines my virtual football experience by striking a deeply satisfying balance between tactical depth and fluid, realistic mechanical execution. The introduction of revamped tactical frameworks completely alters how I approach the pace of play, forcing me to develop a much better understanding of open space, defensive lines, and team positioning on the pitch. This systemic depth makes my build-up play feel incredibly rewarding, especially when I manage to unlock stubborn defensive blocks through patient, precise passing sequences that mirror real-world tactical masterclasses. What really keeps me coming back is the sheer uniqueness of the gameplay loop, alongside the massive evolution of the career mode. I spend hours immersed in the player development menus, customizing specific roles for my squad and navigating complex chemistry webs to get the absolute most out of my team. The overall visual presentation is heavily elevated by authentic match-day audio, and I love how it captures the deafening roar of the stadiums and the distinct, rhythmic sounds of on-pitch action. Backed by extensive licensing and gorgeous, hyper-detailed stadium designs, the game gives me a football simulation that truly captures the high-stakes prestige and tactical beauty of the modern global game.
